key_conditions.condition: the block is frictionless and the object rolls without slipping so mechanical energy is conserved

parts.label: A
accepted_answers: Agree. Both objects lose the same gravitational potential energy. The block converts it all into translational kinetic energy, while the rolling object also has rotational kinetic energy, so less is left for translation.

rubric_rows.criterion: Agrees that the thin spherical shell has a smaller speed
Justifies by stating that both objects lose the same potential energy $mgh$
Explains that part of the energy of the rolling object goes into rotational kinetic energy, leaving less translational kinetic energy
elements: rotational kinetic energy takes some of the energy

parts.label: B
accepted_answers: $mgh=\tfrac12mv^2+\tfrac12(cmR^2)(v/R)^2$ so $v=\sqrt{2gh/(1+c)}$ and $v_r/v_s=1/\sqrt{1+c}\approx0.775$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Writes the energy balance with both translational and rotational terms and $\omega=v/R$
elements: m g h = 1/2 m v^2 + 1/2 I omega^2

rubric_rows.criterion: Obtains $v=\sqrt{2gh/(1+c)}$
Calculates the speed ratio $1/\sqrt{1+c}$ of about 0.775

parts.label: C
accepted_answers: The speed is less, because $v=\sqrt{2gh/(1+c)}$ decreases as $c$ increases and the hoop has the largest possible $c=1$ ($v=\sqrt{gh}$).

rubric_rows.criterion: States that the hoop reaches the bottom with a smaller speed
Justifies with $v=\sqrt{2gh/(1+c)}$ or by saying that a larger fraction of the energy is rotational for the hoop
